progression.startsWith: How can mould reach another piece of bread without the pieces touching?
progression.stopsAfter: Hyphae, sporangial spore release, movement and germination. Explain this asexual route; detailed sexual cycle is deferred.
progression.nextLesson: Yeast budding, the next focused B-fungi delivery part.

teaching.task: Explain how spores travel from a mould colony and start new fungal growth under suitable conditions.
teaching.causalExplanation: The fungal threads obtain nutrients. Mature spore cases release reproductive cells; moving air can carry them to separate food. Water, food and suitable temperature support germination into new threads. Travel and growth are different steps.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Keep recognisable bread and the named mould through the explanation. Plain meanings precede scientific names. A cause is explained before its memory aid.
teaching.openingDecision: How can mould reach another piece of bread without the pieces touching?
teaching.understandingCheck: Explain transport and establishment in a separated-bread arrangement. Complete conditions and demands remain visible during an answer-free hold.
teaching.curriculumScope: Candidate mould contribution only. Yeast budding remains separate and outstanding.
